messages:
incidents-bot: Pager: HIGH severity - private-vpc AcmeCorp GPU queue growth. Queue length 380, GPU utilization 98% across pool 'acme-gpu-01'. Autoscaler attempted 12 scale actions in last 6m, 11 failures. Paging oncall: @alice.oncall :rotating_light:

alice.oncall: Acked. Investigating. First check autoscaler logs and node events.

ben.sre: I see the autoscaler is reporting node create errors: `CreateInstance failed: SubnetIPAddressLimitExceeded` and ephemeral cloud API 429s. Full log snippets below.

ben.sre: ```
2026-03-15T21:12:03Z autoscaler: scaleUpGroup acme-nodegroup-2 -> desired 6 (current 2)
2026-03-15T21:12:04Z cloud-api: CreateInstance acme-nodegroup-2-xyz failed: SubnetHasNoAvailableIPs
2026-03-15T21:12:04Z cloud-api: rateLimit error: 429 TooManyRequests
2026-03-15T21:12:05Z autoscaler: retrying scale action (attempt 2)
```

charlotte.platform: Confirmed - VPC subnet for that private cluster is at 254/256 IPs used, per cloud console. Looks like customer has multiple non-Redwood services in same subnet.

mike.ml: That explains some of the CreateInstance failures. But autoscaler also shows image pull delays causing node notReady for long periods. Example from kubelet on a pending node: `Failed to pull image "redwood-ca:gpu-runtime:2026-01" network timeout`.

ben.sre: Right. So two vectors: IP exhaustion blocking new ENIs and imagepulls delaying node readiness. Combined -> inflight queue stays high and autoscaler keeps hitting max attempts.

ops-bot: Action suggested: 1) open temporary warm capacity fallback (route to shared warm pool), 2) throttle customer burst via rate-limit policy, 3) CS notify customer to move non-critical workloads or open additional subnet IPs.

alice.oncall: I'll start with fallback and rate-limit. ben, can you kick off the warm-pool route? charlotte, can you engage with cloud team to raise subnet IP limits or propose quick mitigation (eg move RW nodes to different subnet)? sam.cs, pls prepare customer-facing note.

ben.sre: Executing route change to warm pool now. Command: ```sh
# add routing rule to prefer warm pool for acme cluster
redwood-cli cluster route set --cluster acme-private-01 --prefer warm-pool-acme --reason "autoscale ip exhaustion"
```

deploy-bot: deploy accepted, warmed instances: 8 GPUs from warm-pool-acme reserved.

ben.sre: Route change applied. Traffic shifting ~20% so far. Queue dropped by ~18 after initial switch.

alice.oncall: Enabling temporary customer throttling to reduce burst. Command applied: `rl-policy apply acme-private-01 --burst 200 --sustained 30/s --duration 60m`

sam.cs: Drafting customer message: "We're seeing IP-address exhaustion in your VPC subnet which is blocking node provisioning. We've applied temporary throttles and routed some traffic to our warm pool while we coordinate with you and cloud provider. CS will DM ops contact for immediate subnet check." Ready to send on approval.

charlotte.platform: Contacted cloud infra. Cloud support says they can lift soft limit quickly but need customer approval to add secondary CIDR or increase subnet size - ETA 1h if customer ok. Also suggested short term: create nodes in a different subnet in same AZ and attach route; requires cluster config tweak.

mike.ml: Meanwhile, I can push a lightweight fallback model to reduce GPU memory usage per request and increase throughput temporarily. Will push canary to warm pool only.

ben.sre: Observed another failure that may be slowing start: CNI plugin occasionally failing to allocate IPs due to race on ENI attach. Logs: 
```
E0305 21:14:03.123 kubelet: failed to setup network for pod "gpu-init": could not allocate IP: AttachNetworkInterface: ENI attach rate limit
```

alice.oncall: OK timeline: 21:12 pager, 21:18 warm-pool routing applied, 21:21 throttles applied, 21:24 CS notified customer. Current status: queue 210 -> still above target but stabilizing. Warm pool handling ~35% of new requests.

sam.cs: Customer (AcmeCorp SRE contact) responded: they have a legacy batch job spiking allocations in that subnet, moving/pausing it. They're going to approve a /21 secondary CIDR - will confirm in ~20-30m. They asked for ETA for full restoration.

charlotte.platform: If customer approves secondary CIDR, we can create nodes in new subnet and autoscaler should succeed. Advise to keep throttles for 30-60m after that to let warm pool drain gracefully.

mike.ml: Canary fallback model is live on warm pool - throughput per GPU increased ~1.4x for smaller prompts. May help reduce cost during recovery.

ben.sre: I've also increased autoscaler retry backoff to reduce API pressure: `autoscaler.conf: cloud_api_max_retries=8 backoff_ms=1200` applied to acme cluster controller. This helps avoid hammering cloud API while customer coordinates changes.

deploy-bot: Config patch applied to cluster-controller acme-private-01 at 21:30.

alice.oncall: Next steps checklist:
- [x] Apply warm-pool routing
- [x] Apply throttles
- [x] CS engaged with customer
- [x] Autoscaler backoff increased
- [x] Canary fallback model deployed
- [ ] Customer approval for secondary CIDR / node subnet expansion (pending)
- [ ] Validate node creation success after subnet change
- [ ] Remove throttles and revert traffic once queue < 50 and stable for 10m

ben.sre: Note for postmortem: autoscaler should detect IP exhaustion errors and switch to fallback faster (hot-path to warm-pool) + we need a health metric that surfaces ongoing cloud API 429s per cluster.

alice.oncall: Agreed. I'll keep the channel open for live updates. If customer confirms subnet expansion, we'll coordinate node creation and then gradually remove throttles. If not, escalate to infra procurement for alternative warm capacity.

sam.cs: Sending customer-facing update now.

mike.ml: Monitoring GPU queue and model qps. Will post perf numbers every 5m.

charlotte.platform: Cloud support assigned case #CS-12478. ETA for soft limit lift if customer ok: 45m.

ben.sre: Current snapshot 21:35: queue=168, gpu-util=92%, warmpool-share=40%. Autoscaler attempts paused to avoid more 429s.

alice.oncall: Thanks team. If there are new failures or customer impact widens, escalate to P1. For now hold operations and I'll update after customer confirmation.

deploy-bot: Canary fallback model ver redwood-fallback-0.3 promoted to warm-pool-acme at 21:28.

incidents-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-03015-ACME-VPC-IP-EXHAUSTION. Channel will remain open for updates.

[later]
sam.cs: Customer confirmed they approved adding secondary CIDR at 22:02 and paused their batch job.

charlotte.platform: Creating nodes in new subnet now, autoscaler allowed to proceed.

ben.sre: Nodes started provisioning. kube events show nodes joining and GPU driver install logs: ```
2026-03-15T22:08:12Z node-01: nvidia-driver install ok
2026-03-15T22:09:54Z node-01: kubelet RegisterNode OK
```

alice.oncall: Monitoring queue. Current 22:12 snapshot: queue=42, gpu-util=68%, warmpool-share=12%. Gradually removing throttles: setting sustained to 60/s for next 15m.

mike.ml: Rolling back fallback model to reduce memory fragmentation. Traffic weight shifted back to primary models.

sam.cs: Sent final customer update with actions taken and recommended follow-ups (move heavy batch jobs to different subnet, request soft quota increase). Customer acknowledged and thanked team.

alice.oncall: Incident de-escalation: Queue under threshold and cluster healthy. Moving incident to postmortem queue. Assigning action items: ben (autoscaler detection improvements), charlotte (playbook for subnet exhaustion), sam (customer guidance template).

ben.sre: I'll start a detailed error-timeline and raise PR for autoscaler fallback.

incidents-bot: Incident status => RESOLVED (monitored) at 22:35."
